questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Potassium superoxide on hydrolysis gives
questions.solution:
On combustion in excess of air, lithium forms mainly the oxide, Li2O (plus some peroxide Li2O2 ), sodium forms the peroxide, Na2O2 (and some superoxide NaO2 ) whilst potassium, rubidium and caesium form the superoxides, MO2. Under appropriate conditions pure compounds M2O, M2O2 and MO2 may be prepared. The increasing stability of the peroxide or superoxide, as the size of the metal ion increases, is due to the stabilisation of large anions by larger cations through lattice energy effects.

Potassium superoxide on hydrolysis gives potassium hydroxide,hydrogen peroxide and oxygen.

2KO2+2H2O→2KOH+H2O2+O2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The alkaline earth metal sulphate, which has its hydration enthalpy greater than its lattice energy is
questions.solution:
Beryllium sulphate has its hydration enthalpy greater than its lattice enthalpy. Hence, it is highly soluble in water. On moving down the group from Be to Ra, the magnitude of hydration enthalpy decreases significantly, due to increase in the atomic radius of alkaline earth metals, bringing about a decrease in solubility of their sulphates. 

If the magnitude of lattice energy is higher than hydration energy then ionic compound is insoluble in water. Whereas if the magnitude of hydration energy is higher than lattice energy, then ionic compound is soluble in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of electrical conductivity of alkali metals ions in their aqueous solution for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Cs</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Na</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math> is
questions.solution:
Lithium cation has the smallest size. So, it is hydrated the most. The size increases down the group. The small size has the more degree of hydration. So, they can not move easily. But the larger cation can move easily. So, they have more mobility.

Hence, the correct order of electrical conductivity of alkali metals ions in their aqueous solution is Cs+>K+>Na+>Li+.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs shows diagonal relationship?
questions.solution:
A diagonal relationship is said to exist between certain pairs of diagonally adjacent elements in the 2nd and 3rd periods.
(a) Li shows diagonal relationship with Mg. Due to comparable :
Electronegativities
$\mathrm{Li}=1.0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}=1.20$
(b) Atomic size, i.e. atomic radii (in pm)
$\mathrm{H}=152 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}=160$
(c) Atomic volume
$\mathrm{Li}=12.97 \mathrm{~mL} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{Mg}=13.97 \mathrm{~mL}$
Thus, Li-resembles $\mathrm{Mg}$ in many respects.

questions.q: What is the increasing order of hydration enthalpies of alkali metal ions?
questions.solution:
Hydration enthalpy described as the amount of energy released on dilution of one mole of gaseous ions.
Alkali metals are highly hydrated and the extent of hydration decreases down the group.
The charge density is more for smaller ions and hence, the smaller ions have higher values of hydration enthalpy. Therefore, increasing order of hydration enthalpies of alkali metals.
$\mathrm{Cs}^{+} \lt  \mathrm{Rb}^{+} \lt  \mathrm{K}^{+} \lt  \mathrm{Na}^{+} \lt  \mathrm{Li}^{+}$

questions.q:
Predict the feasibility of the given reactions in aqueous solution
(i) $\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_4\right]^{2-}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+2 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_4\right]^{2+}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ is amphoteric and the basic strength increases down the group. Due to small size and high ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Be}, \mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ is amphoteric.
Therefore, it dissolves both in acid and bases.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+2 \mathrm{HCl}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Be}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2 \\
& \mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+\mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{BeO}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\
& \mathrm{Or} \mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_4\right] \text { or Be}(\mathrm{OH})_2+2 \mathrm{O} \mathrm{H} \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{OH})_4\right]^{2-}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, both reaction are feasible.

options: $(A)$ is true, $(R)$ is true and $(R)$ is the correct explanation for $(A)$
$(A)$ is true, $(R)$ is true but $(R)$ is not the correct explanation for $(A)$.
questions.solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion. Alcohol forms hydrogen bonding and it also has a covalent character, so it is a polar solvent. So, due to polar nature lithium chloride and magnesium chloride are soluble in polar solvent alcohol. Due to diagonal relationship, $\mathrm{Li}$ and $\mathrm{Mg}$ show many similarity in properties like electronegativities, harder weak bases etc. But this is not a correct explanation of their solubility in alcohol.

questions.q:
Match the following
A B C D
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3-$ Hydrogen bonding Boron is attached to three $\mathrm{O}$-atoms and each oxygen is bonded to one hydrogen, each such unit is $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3$.
(B) $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ - Dimeric form $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ form dimer and exist as $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_6 \cdot \mathrm{AlCl}_3$ is an electron deficient compound, thus behave as Lewis acid.
(C) $\mathrm{B}_3 \mathrm{~N}_3 \mathrm{H}_6$ - Inorganic benzene $\mathrm{B}_3 \mathrm{~N}_3 \mathrm{H}_6$ (Borazine) is a polar inorganic cyclic compound, three $\mathrm{BH}$ units and three $\mathrm{NH}$ units alternate.
(D) $\mathrm{BF}_3-$ Back bonding The exchange of electrons between an atomic orbital on one atom and an antibonding orbital on another atom is known as back bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct statements are
I. The low solubility of LiF is due to its high lattice enthalpy.
II. LiBr is not soluble in acetone.
III. LiCl is soluble in pyridine.
IV. The order of melting points of alkali metal halides is $M F\gt M C l\gt M B r\gt M I$.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Li}^{+}$has high hydration enthalpy but it has high lattice enthalpy in LiF. The lattice enthalpy is higher than hydration enthalpy resulting into low solubility. LiCl is covalent due to small size of cation and large size of anion.
So, it is non-polar and due to better solute-solvent interaction, $\mathrm{LiCl}$ is soluble in pyridine.
In alkali metal halides, the melting point decreases with increase in covalent character which increases with the size of anion in ionic compound. So, the order of melting point is

M F>M C l>M B r>M I

Hence, the correct statements are I, III and IV.

questions.q: Solvay process is used in the manufacture of
questions.solution:
Solvay process is used in the manufacture of sodium carbonate, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$. This process involves following reactions.
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{HCO}_3 \\& \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{HCO}_3+\mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaHCO}_3+\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl} \\& \hline \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \\&+\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}
\end{aligned}$
The sodium bicarbonate obtained on heating gives sodium carbonate.
$\mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2$
Note: This process cannot be used in the manufacture of potassium carbonate as potassium bicarbonate is soluble in the solution of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ and KCl.

The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the
correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is not true
(A) is not true but (R) is true
questions.solution: Superoxides are the species having an $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond and $\mathrm{O}$ in an oxidation state of $-\frac{1}{2}$ (superoxide ion is $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$). Usually these are formed by active metals such as $\mathrm{KO}_2, \mathrm{RbO}_2$ and $\mathrm{CsO}_2$. For the salts of larger anions (like $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$), lattice energy increases in a group. Since, lattice energy is the driving force for the formation of an ionic compound and its stability, the stability of the superoxides from ' $\mathrm{K}$ ' to 'Cs' also increases.

(C) $\mathrm{O}_2$
(D) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
questions.solution:
On hydrolysis of $\mathrm{NaO}_2$ (a superoxide of sodium ), it gives $\mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{NaOH}$ as products. i.e.

Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.
